QUOTE: `mbedtls_ct_compiler_opaque(x)` returns `x` through `asm volatile("" : "+r"(x))` when assembly is available. Otherwise it returns `x ^ mbedtls_ct_zero`... The stated purpose is that the compiler cannot prove the value at compile time, so it cannot fold the mask back into a branch.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer names the empty `asm volatile("" : "+r"(x))` with a read-write register operand and says it serves as an opacity barrier against compiler optimisation.
